task: Horizon 25 of the FeatureSync dashboard: put the dashboard's UI state (flag filter text and which flag rows are open) in the URL query string rendered server-side so a page is bookmarkable and survives a form submit; build the server-side flag filter on top of that contract while keeping the in-browser instant filter as progressive enhancement; and add a sticky Section Nav. Write POSTs keep re-rendering inline with 200/400/422 and draft values — redirect-after-POST is rejected.

analysis.objective: Move the FeatureSync dashboard's UI state — the flag filter text and which flag rows are open — into a server-rendered query-string contract on the environment page, rebuild the flag filter server-side on top of it while keeping the in-browser instant filter as progressive enhancement, and add a sticky Section Nav, so the environment page is bookmarkable and survives a write POST.
analysis.successDefinition: Done when: (1) a single URL-State contract module in packages/dashboard owns the query-string keys (filter text, open flag keys, and the existing version page/pageSize) — no flag-list paging key is added — parses them with the established strict-parse/HttpError(400) style for the numeric keys and leniently for the rest, caps and deduplicates the lenient inputs, and re-serialises them through one helper consistent with flagPath/versionsPath; (2) GET of THE ENVIRONMENT PAGE renders filter text and flag-row open/closed state purely from the query string with no JS required, and copying that URL into a fresh browser reproduces the same rendered state — the flag page, the versions page and collapsible page-sections are explicitly NOT covered and stay deferred; (3) every write POST (feature edit, feature delete, rollout set/remove, segment attach, new flag, publish, rollback) still re-renders inline with 200/400/422 with draft values, notices and field-granular replay behaviour unchanged, and each such form echoes the URL state so the re-rendered page preserves filter and open rows; (4) the flag list is filtered server-side with documented matching semantics reproducing today's browser rule including its two known quirks, the client-side live filter in app.js is RETAINED as progressive enhancement over the already-filtered set (not removed), and flag-list.spec.ts covers both the server submit-and-render flow and the retained instant filtering; flag paging is recorded as deliberately not built; (5) a sticky Section Nav renders on the environment page with links that carry the URL state, styled via a per-feature sheet registered in STYLE_FILES; (6) pnpm verify is green with 100% line/branch/function/statement coverage over packages/*/src/**/*.ts, lint/layer rules clean, and the Playwright suite (including at least one spec proving bookmarkability and open-rows-survive-submit) passes with retries:0.
assumptions: Redirect-after-POST is off the table by user instruction; state travels through hidden form fields and/or form action query strings, and the horizon-23 'every POST collapses every <details>' workaround is retired by server-rendered openness rather than by redirecting.

Open/closed state covers the per-flag <details class="flag-row"> rows on the environment page only, encoded as a bounded, deduplicated, length-capped list of flag keys so the query string cannot grow without limit. Page-level sections are NOT collapsible today and are deferred; nested rollout/segment panels stay client-controlled.

Server-side filter reproduces today's composite client match (key, type, on|off, lowercased, whitespace-split terms, AND, substring) so behaviour does not regress; the client-side live filter is kept as progressive enhancement layered over the server-filtered set (user decision), not removed; an unmatched filter renders the existing empty-state, never an error.
The query-string module horizon 24 deferred as premature is now justified, since three pages read overlapping keys.
Flag paging is treated as conditional: flags all come from one already-read snapshot, so paging is a UI/scroll win at best and is built only if the horizon has room after items 3 and 4.

Unknown or malformed query values fail the established way — strict parse to HttpError(400) for numeric page params, lenient ignore for unknown open-ids and over-long filter text — and are tested in the same phase they are written.
app.js stays outside the coverage gate per the horizon-18 decision, so any logic moved off it lands in covered .ts view modules; no new app.js logic is added.
The existing e2e seed (3 flags, 1 version) may need a few more seeded flags to exercise filtering/paging; enlarging it is in scope only to the extent existing specs' counts must be updated.
risks: Blast radius: roughly six view/form modules plus three POST handlers in http-server.ts must echo state; a single form left un-echoed silently loses filter/open state and is easy to miss without a per-form test.

Rejecting POST-redirect-GET means state correctness now depends on hand-written hidden inputs in every form, which is the fragile path; the compensating control is an exhaustive per-form test asserting the echoed fields.

The 100% branch gate over hand-written HTML strings — already a standing open blocker — gets materially harder with filter/open-state conditionals in every view; test files may balloon or the gate may force awkward view shapes.

Encoding open flag rows in the URL is an unbounded-input surface: without a hard cap on count and value length, a crafted URL becomes a cheap render-amplification/DoS vector and a long-URL 414 source.

Filter text and flag keys flow into HTML and into form action URLs, so any path missing escapeHtml/encodeURIComponent is an injection defect; existing escape helpers must be used on every new emission point.
flag-list.spec.ts is being replaced rather than extended; if the rewrite is weaker than the original, loss of live-filter coverage will not be visible to the coverage gate (e2e is excluded from it).
Scope overflow is likely at six-to-eight phases; Section Nav is the designated drop, but dropping it after its CSS/markup is half-landed would leave dead STYLE_FILES entries.
Server-rendered openness can fight app.js's existing details.open = true replay behaviour, producing rows that reopen or refuse to close; ownership must be decided once, not per page.
Open blockers about the concurrent-replay 200+422 race and the pointer-read window remain unresolved; touching every write form raises the chance of tripping that flakiness in CI.
outOfScope: Redirect-after-POST / POST-redirect-GET for any write handler — explicitly rejected by the user; inline 200/400/422 re-render with draft values and field-granular replay must not change.
Any change to edit, publish, rollback or replay semantics, including the unresolved 200+422 concurrent-replay race — this horizon moves UI state, not write behaviour.
Segment List filtering, paging or URL state — only flags and versions are in the contract; segments stay as horizon 23/24 left them.
Version-index or bucket-listing shortcuts — the horizon-24 decision that version history is paged arithmetically from the Current Pointer stands.
New client-side behaviour in app.js — app.js is outside the coverage gate, so logic moves to the server rather than growing there.
Fixing the double snapshot read per environment-page render (browseEnvironment + listPublishedSegments) — a known read-cost discovery, but a separate performance concern.
Retiring the dead listReferencedSegments module and other recorded tech debt — unrelated cleanup that would dilute this horizon's diff.
Visual redesign, theming or responsive rework of the dashboard beyond the sticky Section Nav's own per-feature stylesheet.
Authentication, authorization or sharing semantics for bookmarkable URLs — the dashboard's existing Origin/Host localhost guard is unchanged.

URL state on the flag page and the versions page, and collapsible page-level sections — the success bar was deliberately narrowed to the environment page at the alignment checkpoint so the horizon can pass its own bar.
Removing the client-side live filter from app.js — the user chose to keep it as progressive enhancement over the server-filtered list, so no UX regression and no loss of its existing e2e coverage.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective is about the dashboard's HTTP/URL plumbing and server-side rendering machinery — query-string parsing, form round-trips, view markup and nav chrome — not about flag, segment or snapshot domain rules, which are untouched.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: The dashboard's UI state carried in the query string (filter text, open sections, open flag rows, page numbers) and rendered server-side.
The single module owning the key spellings, value grammar, parsing, clamping and re-serialisation of URL State, shared by the environment, flag and versions pages.
The server-side substring match over a flag's key, type and on/off state that selects which flag rows are rendered; successor to the app.js live filter.
Which page sections and per-flag <details> rows render expanded, decided by URL State instead of by the browser or app.js.
The hidden form fields and/or form action query string by which a write POST carries URL State through an inline re-render, with no redirect.
The sticky in-page navigation strip on dashboard pages whose links carry URL State forward.
The per-flag GET route added in horizon 24 (flagPath) that URL State deep-links into.
The CI-enforced 100% line/branch/function/statement threshold over packages/*/src/**/*.ts that every new view branch must satisfy in the phase that writes it.
The URL State Contract subsystem of the dashboard — the pipeline stage this horizon's phase of that name delivers.

discoveryFindings.finding: dispatch() builds new URL(String(request.url), 'http://localhost'), splits pathname into non-empty segments, then calls match(segments, request.method). The URL object (including url.searchParams) is passed as the 3rd arg to route.handle, so every handler already has query access — but only 4 handlers use it: home ('env'), /changes ('since','edited'), /versions ('page','pageSize'). All POST handlers take only (request, response) and ignore the URL entirely.
discoveryFindings.implication: No new plumbing is needed to read the query string in POST handlers: just add the url param to their handle signatures. Form-action query strings are therefore the cheaper echo mechanism than hidden fields for handlers, though hidden fields are needed for the fields readForm() sees. Plan should pick one and state it, since both are already available.

discoveryFindings.finding: match() has a hard guard: if (segments[0] !== 'env' || segments.length < 2 || segments.length > 4) return undefined. Everything is keyed off segments.length (2/3/4) plus segments[2] equality. Branch order: [] home, STYLESHEET_PATH, CLIENT_SCRIPT_PATH, guard, len2 env page, current-version, changes, merge, merge/apply, publish, rollback, features (create), features/:key (POST editRoute else GET flag page), matchSegmentRoute, versions (list), versions/:n, undefined.
discoveryFindings.implication: Any new route must fit within 2-4 segments. Adding URL state needs no routing change at all — it is query-string only, the lowest-risk shape.

discoveryFindings.finding: Two parsers exist. parseVersion(value): /^[1-9]\d{0,8}$/ else throw new HttpError(400,'The version must be a positive integer.'). parsePageNumber(value, fallback, message): null -> fallback, else same regex or HttpError(400) with PAGE_MESSAGE / PAGE_SIZE_MESSAGE. parseBaseVersion(fields) is the lenient sibling: same regex but returns undefined on failure, which callers convert into a 400/422 inline draft failure with BASE_VERSION_MESSAGE.
discoveryFindings.implication: The URL-state module should reuse exactly these two idioms: strict-throw for numeric page keys, lenient-ignore for open-ids and filter text. The regex caps at 9 digits, so clamping happens downstream in listVersionPage (clamp to 1..MAX_VERSION_PAGE_SIZE=50), not in the parser. A new contract module must decide where clamping lives and stay consistent.

discoveryFindings.finding: Five POST re-render surfaces in http-server.ts: (a) editRoute, a factory used twice — POST /env/:e/features (create, draftState -> {createDraft}) and POST /env/:e/features/:key (edit, draftState -> {editDraft}); it re-renders renderEnvironmentPage(view, state) with 200 success / 400 when outcome.invalidInput===true / 422 otherwise; (b) POST /publish echoes draft + conflict; (c) POST /rollback no draft; (d) POST /merge returns a fragment; (e) POST /merge/apply returns JSON 200/409. Plus segment-routes.ts has POST /segments and POST /segments/:key.
discoveryFindings.implication: The brief's 'three POST handlers' undercounts: editRoute is one factory but two routes, plus publish and rollback = 4 environment-page re-renders that must re-render URL state. merge/merge-apply are fragment/JSON and need no state. Segment POSTs are out of scope, so they need no echo — the plan should say so to avoid a reviewer flagging them.

discoveryFindings.finding: There is no single helpers module. environmentPath(environment) lives in views/escape.ts alongside escapeHtml. flagPath(environment, key) lives in views/flag-page.ts = environmentPath(e) + '/features/' + encodeURIComponent(key) — no query params. versionsPath(environment, page = 1) lives in views/version-list-page.ts and appends bare '?page=' with no merging of other keys — the only helper that appends a query. segmentListPath in segment-list-page.ts, segmentPath in segment-page.ts. feature-edit-form.ts and new-flag-form.ts build their form actions inline rather than calling flagPath.
discoveryFindings.implication: versionsPath's '?page=' must be refactored to compose with the new contract or the version pager will drop filter/open state. feature-edit-form's inline action duplicates flagPath's expression — the most likely place state gets lost. Path helpers are scattered across 5 files; centralising them is a natural companion to the contract module.

discoveryFindings.finding: 20 modules under views/ with line counts: error-page 4, client-script 10, escape 12, home-page 13, stylesheet 15, version-page 31, segment-page 40, new-flag-form 41, flag-page 44, snapshot-contents 47, layout 50, segment-attach-form 55, changes-dialog 64, version-list-page 69, feature-edit-form 82, segment-list-page 85, merge-dialog 91, rollout-form 99, environment-page 165. Plus scripts/app.js 315 and 10 CSS files.
discoveryFindings.implication: Nine of these render a form. Modules are small (<=165 lines); a new url-state.ts of ~60-100 lines fits the convention. environment-page.ts at 165 is the largest and is where Section Nav, filter and section-openness all land — it will need splitting or it becomes the new god view.

discoveryFindings.area: forms — exact actions and hidden inputs
discoveryFindings.finding: Every form and what it emits: (1) feature-edit-form.ts action=/env/<e>/features/<key> hidden baseVersion, submit buttons name=field. (2) same file delete form, same action, hidden baseVersion, field=delete. (3) rollout-form.ts detach form, hidden baseVersion + ruleIndex, field=detachSegment. (4) rollout-form.ts rollout form, hidden baseVersion + ruleIndex + percentage/bucketBy/salt. (5) segment-attach-form.ts, hidden baseVersion, select segmentKey. (6) new-flag-form.ts action=/env/<e>/features hidden baseVersion. (7) environment-page.ts publish form action=/env/<e>/publish hidden baseVersion. (8) version-list-page.ts rollback form action=/env/<e>/rollback hidden version. (9) merge dialogs method=dialog close forms. (10) home-page.ts method=get action=/. Segment forms in segment-list-page.ts and segment-page.ts.
discoveryFindings.implication: Eight write forms need state echo (1-8). baseVersionInput() in feature-edit-form.ts is already the established pattern for a hidden input every form threads through — feature-edit-form passes it as a string into renderRolloutForms and renderSegmentAttachForm. Mirroring it with a required stateInputs()/stateQuery() param makes 'a form left un-echoed' a compile error rather than a silent bug.

discoveryFindings.finding: For each [data-filter] input: list = querySelector('.' + data-filter); empty = list.parentNode.querySelector('[data-filter-empty]'); input.hidden = false (the input is rendered hidden server-side and revealed only by JS). On 'input': terms = value.trim().toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean); for each [data-search] item, match = terms.every(term => text.indexOf(term) !== -1); item.hidden = !match; empty.hidden = shown !== 0. The haystack is the data-search attribute built in snapshot-contents.ts: (flag.key + ' ' + flag.type + ' ' + (flag.enabled ? 'on' : 'off')).toLowerCase().
discoveryFindings.implication: The server-side filter must reproduce: whitespace-split into terms, AND across terms, case-insensitive substring (indexOf, not word-boundary), over exactly key + ' ' + type + ' ' + on|off. There is a pre-existing quirk: the term 'on' matches 'off' by substring and also matches 'config'. Documenting the matching semantics must own that quirk explicitly — keep it, or fix it and note the behaviour change.

discoveryFindings.finding: Two places force openness. In restore(): var details = field.closest('details'); while (details) { details.open = true; details = details.parentElement.closest('details'); } — walks every ancestor details open for each carried-over edit field. In the changesBody click handler for inConflict() + 'keep': row.querySelector('details').open = true; row.scrollIntoView.
discoveryFindings.implication: This is the direct conflict the brief warns about. Both paths run AFTER the server renders openness from the URL, so client-forced-open wins and rows the URL says are closed pop open when a carried edit touches them. Decide once: keep the client force-open as an additive override and accept URL/DOM divergence, or have these paths rewrite history.replaceState — but the latter is new app.js logic, which is forbidden. The additive override is the only consistent option.

discoveryFindings.area: page sections are NOT collapsible today
discoveryFindings.finding: The 'Flags' and 'Version history' blocks are plain <section class="section" aria-labelledby="flags-heading"> / versions-heading with a <div class="section-head">. They are always expanded — there is no details element at page-section level anywhere. layout.css only gives .section a margin-top and .section-head a flex row. The only details on the environment page are .flag-row per flag, .rollouts, .segment-attach, .danger-zone delete, the rules editor, the New flag card and Raw JSON.
discoveryFindings.implication: 'Which page sections are open or closed' is a NEW capability, not a relocation: the plan must first convert the two sections into collapsible disclosures (markup + CSS + tests) before URL state can control them. That is a distinct phase from flag-row openness, and a candidate to cut if the horizon overflows — flag-row openness is the one that actually retires the horizon-23 workaround.

discoveryFindings.finding: Server-side openness is per-draft only: snapshot-contents.ts const open = editable.draft?.key === flag.key ? ' open' : ''; feature-edit-form.ts <details${draft?.rulesJson === undefined ? '' : ' open'}>; new-flag-form.ts <details class="card"${draft === undefined ? '' : ' open'}>. Nothing else ever emits open.
discoveryFindings.implication: URL-driven openness must OR with these existing draft rules, not replace them — a rejected draft must still force its row open even if the URL says closed, or the 400/422 inline-error UX regresses. That is an extra branch, and therefore an extra test, at each of the three sites.

discoveryFindings.finding: The workaround lives in the e2e specs, not in src. segment-upload-rollout.spec.ts clicks '.flag-row > summary' then 'details.rollouts > summary' before asserting; segment-picker.spec.ts has the explicit comment 'The reload after the publish collapses every <details> again, so the flag has to be reopened' followed by two summary clicks. fixtures.ts exports expandFlag(page,key) which encapsulates the first click.
discoveryFindings.implication: Retiring the workaround means editing two LocalStack-backed specs which require LocalStack to run — they cannot be verified in a plain unit run. The nested .rollouts panel would still collapse unless nested panels are in the contract, which they are not. So the workaround only half-retires: the plan should explicitly keep the nested reopen click and say why.

discoveryFindings.finding: stylesheet.ts is 15 lines: STYLE_FILES is a 10-entry as-const array with an ordering comment ('tokens first, then layout, then the components that use both'): base, layout, forms, components, tables, rollout, segments, segment-list, segment-create, segment-attach. STYLESHEET is readFileSync().join. STYLESHEET_PATH='/assets/app.css'; STYLESHEET_HREF appends a 12-char sha256 content hash. Per-feature sheets are tiny: segments.css 12, segment-create.css 12, segment-list.css 13, segment-attach.css 23, rollout.css 34 (vs base 128, components 439).
discoveryFindings.implication: A section-nav.css of ~15-30 lines appended to STYLE_FILES is exactly the established shape. Per the ordering comment a nav sheet belongs after components.css. There is already one position:sticky precedent (.update-banner, top 0.5rem, z-index 10) — the Section Nav must coordinate z-index and top with it or the two stickies overlap.

discoveryFindings.finding: views/escape.ts is 12 lines: an ENTITIES map (& < > " ') and escapeHtml = (value: unknown) => String(value).replace(/[&<>"']/g, ...). There is NO url-encoding helper beyond raw encodeURIComponent, used in exactly 4 places: escape.ts (environmentPath), flag-page.ts (flagPath), segment-page.ts (segmentPath), feature-edit-form.ts (inline action). versionsPath does not encode its page number. Every href/action/value emission wraps the whole URL in escapeHtml — that double layer is the house pattern.
discoveryFindings.implication: Filter text and flag keys entering query strings need BOTH layers. Safest: build the query with URLSearchParams.toString() (which percent-encodes) then escapeHtml the whole URL — otherwise the & separators get double-escaped or the filter text leaks a quote into an attribute. An existing test ('HTML-escapes environment names, flag keys and values, including in attributes' with encodeURIComponent of a script tag and quotes) is the template for the new escaping tests.

discoveryFindings.finding: http-server.test.ts is 1714 lines, ~80 it() cases in nested describes per route, with helpers call(dashboard, method, path, body?) and form(fields) => new URLSearchParams(fields).toString(). Co-located view tests: environment-page.test.ts 92, flag-page.test.ts 96, version-list-page.test.ts 105, dialogs.test.ts 103, rollout-form.test.ts 168, segment-attach-form.test.ts 173, segment-list-page.test.ts 184, feature-edit-form.test.ts 395. They build literal view fixtures and assert on the HTML string via regex extraction. Application tests live under test/application/, NOT co-located; infrastructure tests ARE co-located.
discoveryFindings.implication: Convention is clear: a new url-state.ts under src/infrastructure gets a co-located url-state.test.ts. Per-form echo assertions belong in the co-located view tests (cheap, no server) while the round-trip belongs in http-server.test.ts, already 1714 lines and growing. Budget for that growth explicitly.

discoveryFindings.finding: Only 4 specs: flag-list.spec.ts 44, segment-picker.spec.ts 77, segment-upload-rollout.spec.ts 77, concurrent-edits.spec.ts 101. flag-list.spec.ts has 3 tests; the live-filter test fills the searchbox and asserts page.locator('[data-flag]').filter({visible:true}) counts — fill('dark') -> 1 visible, fill('boolean on') -> 1 visible, fill('nothing-like-this') -> 'No flags match.' visible. playwright.config.ts: testDir 'e2e', fullyParallel, retries 0, timeout 30s, trace/screenshot/video all off (deliberately, because CSVs carry personal data).
discoveryFindings.implication: Rewriting flag-list.spec.ts server-side means visibility assertions become presence/absence assertions (filtered rows are no longer rendered at all, so [data-flag] count, not filter({visible:true})). 'boolean on' currently yields exactly 1 and depends on the 3-flag seed; if the seed grows that assertion must be recomputed. retries:0 plus trace:off means new flakiness is hard to debug — argues for few, deterministic new e2e assertions.

discoveryFindings.finding: e2e/support/fixtures.ts is 113 lines. InMemoryEnvironment holds snapshots: string[], currentVersion = snapshots.length, publish() enforces the same CAS as S3 (throws S3PublishError/CONFLICT), publishAs(createdBy, features, reason). ports() returns DashboardPorts with readCurrentVersion, fetchSnapshotText, listPublishedSegments -> {status:'listed', segments: []}, publishSegment and openWriter().rollback as rejecting stubs, readSegmentVersion -> null. SEED has exactly 3 flags: new-dashboard (boolean, enabled), checkout-limits (config, disabled, default {max:3}), dark-mode (boolean, disabled), published once -> exactly 1 version. Exports checkForUpdates(page) and expandFlag(page,key).
discoveryFindings.implication: 3 flags / 1 version. Flag paging over 3 flags is unjustifiable without enlarging SEED, and enlarging SEED breaks concurrent-edits.spec.ts which spreads ...SEED in four places and asserts on published feature maps. Strong evidence for recording flag paging as deliberately not built. Also openWriter().rollback rejects, so the rollback POST cannot be exercised e2e at all — its state echo must be covered by http-server.test.ts only.

discoveryFindings.finding: Root vitest.config.ts (28 lines) builds one project per packages/* dir, each excluding integration/** and e2e/**. coverage: provider v8, include ['packages/*/src/**/*.ts'], exclude ['**/*.test.ts'], thresholds lines/branches/functions/statements all 100. No per-file overrides, no exclusions for view modules.
discoveryFindings.implication: app.js is outside the gate (it is .js and include is *.ts), e2e is outside it, and every new ternary in a view template is a branch that must be hit in the same phase. The include glob also means a new src/infrastructure/url-state.ts is gated from the moment it exists — the plan must not land it un-tested even as a stub.

discoveryFindings.finding: browseEnvironment(ports, environment) returns EnvironmentView = {environment, status, currentVersion, versions: VersionEntry[], current: SnapshotVersionView}. Flags arrive NOT pre-sliced: the full flag list is built in readContents() from Object.entries(parsed.value.features).map(...) into SnapshotContents.flags. It reads a window of min(currentVersion, ENVIRONMENT_VERSION_WINDOW=5) versions in parallel. renderSnapshotContents(contents, editable?) and the module-private renderFlagCard(flag, editable) are the render seam; renderSnapshotContents also has the non-editable table branch (renderTableRow) reused by version-page.ts.
discoveryFindings.implication: Filtering/slicing can happen in the application layer (a pure filterFlags over SnapshotContents.flags, testable without HTML) or inside renderSnapshotContents. The former is far better for the 100% branch gate and matches the list-version-page.ts precedent (clamp + slice in application, render in view). But renderSnapshotContents is shared with version-page.ts, which must NOT be filtered — so the filter must apply only to the editable branch, or be a separate parameter defaulted off.

discoveryFindings.finding: Grepped all of packages/dashboard/src: there is no shared query-string, url-state or params module of any kind. URLSearchParams appears only in http-primitives.ts readForm() (parsing POST bodies) and as the type flowing through http-server.ts's form parsers; url.searchParams is read ad-hoc in 4 handlers. decisions.md already records the horizon-24 user decision: 'Filter and open/closed state will live in the query string rendered server-side, never in app.js'.
discoveryFindings.implication: The contract module is genuinely new — nothing to reconcile against, and the architectural decision is already made and recorded, so the first phase need not re-litigate it. There is no precedent for where such a module lives: src/infrastructure/ beside http-primitives.ts is the natural home since it is HTTP plumbing, and views already import from infrastructure siblings.

discoveryFindings.finding: eslint.config.js uses tseslint.configs.strictTypeChecked repo-wide plus import-x/no-restricted-paths with exactly two zones scoped to packages/*/src/**/*.ts: domain must not import application or infrastructure; application must not import infrastructure. There is NO rule restricting infrastructure-to-infrastructure or views-to-infrastructure imports, and none forbidding views importing each other. app.js is separately configured with sourceType script, disableTypeChecked and an explicit global allowlist. Root scripts: lint = eslint . --max-warnings=0; verify = builds 5 packages then typecheck + lint + test --coverage.
discoveryFindings.implication: A url-state module under src/infrastructure/ can be imported freely by http-server.ts and every views/* module — no lint obstacle. But application code may not import it, so if any filtering logic goes into src/application/ then the contract it depends on must live in application or domain. That layering choice must be made in the first phase, not discovered in the fourth. strictTypeChecked also means no any, and URLSearchParams.get() returning string|null must be narrowed explicitly everywhere.

discoveryFindings.finding:
environment-page.ts renders the filter input with a literal hidden attribute and the comment 'Revealed by the page script; without JavaScript every flag simply stays listed.' It is — not inside any form, so it currently cannot submit anything. The empty-state is a sibling

No flags match.

. Both only appear when contents.status==='valid' and flags.length > 0.
discoveryFindings.implication: Server-side filtering requires wrapping this input in a method=get form (a real markup change), dropping the hidden attribute so it works without JS (a behaviour improvement worth asserting), and re-deriving the empty state server-side. The e2e locator getByRole('searchbox', {name: /Filter flags/}) keeps working if aria-label is preserved. A GET form's action plus hidden inputs is the only way to carry the other state keys through the filter submit, so the filter form itself is a state-echo site too — easy to miss.

discoveryFindings.finding: home-page.ts already uses <form method="get" action="/"> with <input name="env">, handled by a route that reads url.searchParams.get('env') and 303-redirects to environmentPath(environment) when non-empty, else renders the home page. A redirect() helper issuing 303 exists.
discoveryFindings.implication: There IS a GET-form plus redirect precedent, so a GET filter form is idiomatic here. The redirect() helper is used only by that one route — the plan should note it stays unused by write POSTs, so no reviewer mistakes the rejected redirect-after-POST for 'the helper already exists, why not use it'.

discoveryFindings.finding: Stable ids already exist for nav anchoring: current-heading, flags-heading, versions-heading, plus publish-dialog, changes-dialog, update-banner, merge-notice, current-json, version-json, snapshot. The sections themselves carry aria-labelledby pointing at those heading ids but have no id of their own.
discoveryFindings.implication: Section Nav links can target #current-heading / #flags-heading / #versions-heading with zero markup churn, or add ids to the sections for a better scroll target. Either way the Section Nav is genuinely markup plus CSS only and depends on nothing the other items produce — confirming it as the clean drop. If built, it should be the LAST phase so dropping it leaves no dead STYLE_FILES entry.

discoveryFindings.finding: No written justification for flag paging exists anywhere in the repo; next-horizon-brief.md and decisions.md discuss it only as an open question. blockers.md and state.md were not read in full, so the exact wording of the unresolved 200+422 concurrent-replay race and pointer-read window blockers is unverified beyond the analysis summary.
discoveryFindings.implication: Per the analysis's own gate ('flag paging ships only if a written justification exists'), no such justification exists today — so the plan should default to recording flag paging as deliberately not built, while the contract module still parses and reserves the key so adding paging later needs no contract change.

phases.name: Add query-string state module for dashboard URLs
phases.goal: Create one module in packages/dashboard that owns the dashboard's URL query-string keys — flag filter text, open flag rows, version page and page size — parsing them from a URL and serialising them back into a query string.
phases.rationale: The dashboard currently reads query parameters ad hoc in four different request handlers with no shared spelling or validation, so the same parameter can be parsed two different ways. One module that both reads and writes these parameters gives every page and link a single agreed contract, and is the foundation every later phase in this horizon builds on.

Do NOT add a flag-list paging key: flag paging is deliberately not built this horizon.

Export parseUrlState(searchParams) that reads the keys 'filter', 'open', 'page' and 'pageSize'; parse 'page'/'pageSize' with the existing strict style used by parsePageNumber in http-server.ts (regex match or throw HttpError(400) with the existing page messages), and parse 'filter'/'open' leniently — never throw, ignore what does not fit.

Bound the lenient inputs: trim filter text and cut it at a fixed maximum length (e.g. 100 characters); split 'open' on commas, drop empty entries, drop entries longer than a fixed key length cap, deduplicate, and keep at most a fixed number (e.g. 20) so a hand-crafted URL cannot grow the render without limit.

Export serialiseUrlState(state) building the query string with URLSearchParams so values are percent-encoded, omitting keys that hold their default value so clean URLs stay clean, and returning '' when nothing needs carrying.

Export withUrlState(path, state) returning path plus '?' plus the serialised query when non-empty; callers wrap the result in the existing escapeHtml helper when it lands in an href or action attribute.

Change versionsPath in views/version-list-page.ts to build its query through serialiseUrlState/withUrlState instead of appending a bare '?page=' string, so the version pager stops being the one hand-rolled query builder.

Add url-state.test.ts covering every branch: defaults, each key present and absent, a rejected non-numeric page (HttpError 400), over-long filter text, over-long/duplicate/empty/over-count 'open' entries, round-trip parse(serialise(state)) equality, and a filter value containing quotes and '&' to prove encoding.

phases.name: Add server-side flag filter function
phases.goal: Add a pure function that takes the list of flags read from a snapshot plus the filter text and returns only the flags that match, reproducing exactly the matching rules the browser script performs today.
phases.rationale: Today filtering happens only in the browser: the server sends every flag and a small script hides the rows that do not match, so the filtered view cannot be bookmarked or survive a form submit. Moving the match rule into a plain, separately testable function is the prerequisite for the server deciding which rows to render, and keeps the rule out of HTML-building code where it would be awkward to test.

phases.name: Open flag rows named in the URL
phases.goal: Make each expandable flag row on the environment page render already expanded when its flag key appears in the URL's list of open rows, while keeping the existing rule that a row with a rejected draft always opens.
phases.rationale: Each flag is an expandable disclosure row, and today the browser decides what is expanded, so every page load and every form submit collapses everything and the user has to click their row open again. Letting the URL say which rows are expanded makes a deep-linked, expanded row bookmarkable and is the change that removes those repeated re-open clicks.

Put a plain link inside each flag row's heading (the <summary>) whose href is the environment path with this row's key added to — or, when the row is already open, removed from — the URL's open list via the state module, preserving the current filter text. It is an ordinary link that reloads the page; the native expand/collapse widget is NOT replaced, so the row still toggles instantly for anyone with JavaScript while the link is what makes the state shareable and submit-surviving.
Percent-encode flag keys through the state module's serialiser and wrap the produced URL in escapeHtml so a key containing quotes or ampersands cannot break out of the attribute.
Leave the nested panels inside a row (rollout rules, segment attach) out of the URL contract; note in a comment that end-to-end tests still click those nested summaries open deliberately.
Add tests for all four combinations of (key in URL open list yes/no) x (draft present yes/no), plus a test that a flag key containing quotes is escaped in the generated link.

phases.name: Carry URL state through every write form
phases.goal: Make every form that writes a change carry the current filter text and open-row list with it, so the page the server renders back after a submit shows the same filtered, expanded view the user was looking at.
phases.rationale: Saving a change re-renders the page in place rather than redirecting, so anything not sent with the form is lost — the user's filter clears and their expanded row collapses. Sending the state with each form is the only way it survives a save, and passing it as a required argument to each form builder makes a forgotten form a compile error instead of a silent loss.
changes: Add a stateInputs(state) helper (mirroring the existing baseVersionInput helper that every form already threads through) that renders the current filter text and open-row list as hidden form inputs, and thread it as a REQUIRED parameter into all eight write forms: feature edit, feature delete, rollout set, rollout detach, segment attach, new flag, publish, rollback.

Also append the serialised state to each form's action URL through the state module, and replace the hand-written inline action string in feature-edit-form.ts with the shared flag path helper so the two cannot drift apart.

Give the POST request handlers that re-render the environment page — the create-flag route, the edit-flag route, publish and rollback — access to the request URL (the dispatcher already passes it; the handlers currently ignore it) and read the echoed state from the submitted form fields so the re-rendered page reapplies the filter and the open rows.

Keep the write behaviour itself untouched: the same inline 200 success / 400 invalid-input / 422 rejected responses, the same draft values, notices and per-field replay. No redirect after a POST is introduced.

Leave the segment create/edit POSTs and the merge dialog/JSON endpoints without state echo — segments are out of this horizon's scope and the merge endpoints return a fragment and JSON, not a page — and record that in a comment so a reviewer does not read it as an omission.

Add a test per form asserting the hidden state inputs and the action URL are present and escaped, plus request-level tests that a POST carrying filter and open-row fields re-renders with that filter applied and that row expanded, for each of the four page-rendering POST routes, at each of the 200 / 400 / 422 outcomes that route can produce.

Budget for test-file growth deliberately: http-server.test.ts is already ~1714 lines and this phase adds per-route, per-outcome state-echo assertions to it. Either add them under a new describe block in that file, or split the state-echo request tests into their own co-located test file — decide before writing, do not let it grow incidentally.

Add an end-to-end browser proof that open rows survive a submit: a new e2e/url-state.spec.ts that opens a flag row, applies a filter, submits the FEATURE EDIT form, and asserts on the re-rendered page that the previously open flag row is still expanded and the filter is still applied. This needs no LocalStack — the in-memory e2e fixture (e2e/support/fixtures.ts, InMemoryEnvironment) already supports the feature-edit POST path. The ROLLBACK form cannot be proven this way because openWriter().rollback is a rejecting stub in that fake, so the rollback route's state echo stays covered by http-server.test.ts only — say so in a comment in the spec rather than omitting it silently.

Retire the horizon-23 re-open workaround where it is now unnecessary: in e2e/segment-picker.spec.ts and e2e/segment-upload-rollout.spec.ts drop the FLAG-ROW re-open click (the server now renders that row open from the URL state) but KEEP the nested panel click on details.rollouts > summary, because nested rollout/segment panels are deliberately outside the URL-State contract per the deferred list. These two specs are LocalStack-backed, so note that they cannot be verified in a plain unit run.

phases.name: Add sticky section navigation strip
phases.goal: Add a small navigation strip to the dashboard pages that stays visible while scrolling and jumps to the page's main sections.
phases.rationale: The environment page is long — current snapshot, flag list, version history — and a user scrolled to the bottom has no quick way back to another section. A strip of in-page links that stays pinned as the page scrolls fixes that. It is purely markup and styling and depends on nothing else in this horizon.

Create a NEW small per-feature stylesheet views/styles/section-nav.css (roughly 15-30 lines, matching the existing per-feature sheets such as rollout.css and segment-attach.css) holding only this component's styles; do not add these rules to any existing stylesheet.
Register 'section-nav.css' in the STYLE_FILES list in stylesheet.ts after components.css, following that file's stated ordering comment (tokens, then layout, then components that use both).
Make the strip stick to the top while scrolling, and pick a top offset and stacking order that do not overlap the existing sticky update banner (which sits at top 0.5rem with stacking order 10).
Render the nav near the top of the environment page body, and add tests asserting the links, their labels, their state-carrying hrefs and that the stylesheet list includes the new file.
